To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the deleterious effects of hyperglycemia on the immune system are dependent on the genetic background.
the susceptibility to the deleterius effect of hyperglycemia on immune response is strain dependent.

(i) the immune response is affected in a mouse strain‐dependent manner in a model of diabetes; (ii) the effect of diabetes is mediated, at least in part, by hyperglycaemia; (iii) the effect of hyperglycemia is dependent upon the mouse strain; (iv) the deleterious effects of hyperglycemic conditions are associated to an oxidative stress.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the immune response in two mouse models of diabetes, BALB/c and C57BL/ 6J, and the participation of hyperglycemia and oxidative stress.
the study of the immunological response in diabetes mellitus.
the development of an experimental model to study the deletrious effect of hyperglucemia over the immune system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the immune system is affected by diabetes in a strain‐dependent manner, and this effect could be mediated by oxidative stress and hyperglycaemia.
diabetes mellitus, as well as hyperglycaemia per se, has a differential effect on the immune response depending on the mouse strain, with a possible implication of oxidative stress.
the genetic background of mice strains is important in determining the susceptibility to develop the deleterious effects of hyperglycaemic stress.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
hyperglycaemia affects the immune response in mice with different genetic background.
the immune response of diabetic mice depends on the genetic background.

the immune response of diabetic BALB/cBy J mice is impaired by the deleterious effects of hyperglycaemic conditions, whereas C57Bl/ 6J mice are resistant to these effects, suggesting that the susceptibility of an animal to develop the complications associated with diabetes may be related to the strain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the immune response is differentially affected by diabetes in mice with different genetic backgrounds.
the genetic background of a mouse strain has to be considered when establishing experimental models for the study of diabetes‐associated complications.
genetic differences between mice strains may be used to identify susceptibility to the development of diabetes‐related complications.
